issues.description: The problem specification defines SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() as returning void (UML and textual description), but the solution implementation declares checkOrderReady() as returning boolean. This return-type mismatch between specification and solution can confuse students about the required signature and expected behavior of the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make checkOrderReady() match the specification by changing its return type to void in the implementation (remove the boolean return value). Adjust the implementation to not return a value and ensure any callers do not rely on a boolean result. Alternatively, update the problem statement to document that checkOrderReady() returns a boolean if that was intended.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize both the orders array and the final stock in the constructor of SealSaloon, but elsewhere (and in the requirements) it explicitly states that the stock attribute must be static. Initializing a static (and final) stock in an instance constructor is contradictory: static fields are class-level and typically initialized at declaration or in a static initializer. This creates confusion about whether stock should be an instance field initialized in the constructor or a static field shared across all instances.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement to consistently state that stock is a static (class-level) final field and should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer, while orders should be initialized in the instance constructor. Update the sentence that currently instructs students to initialize stock in the constructor to only refer to initializing orders there.
